readerTitle: Why six customers can beat 40,000 sign-ups
caseNote: 가상 사례 (산업용 철제 운반 랙 제조사 vs 무료 일정 관리 앱, 핫소스 브랜드) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 트랙션은 숫자의 크기가 아니라 증거의 무게다. 고객이 대가를 치르고 다시 돌아왔는지, 그 선이 어느 방향으로 가는지가 핵심이다.
misconception: 가입자 수, 팔로워, 언론 보도, 입점 매장 수처럼 큰 숫자가 곧 트랙션이다.

sources.text: 창업·투자 실무의 일반 개념 (트랙션, 리텐션, 고객 집중 위험)

factChecks.note: 차트 계산 확인: 랙 제조사 재주문 고객 5 ÷ 6 = 83.3%(83%로 표기), 앱 주간 활성 사용자 800 ÷ 40,000 = 2%. 모두 가상 수치입니다.
핫소스 사례의 120개 매장, 재주문율 70%, 팔로워 50,000명은 모두 설명용 가상 수치입니다.
'letter of intent'를 '구매를 검토하겠다는 서면 약속'으로 단순화해 풀었습니다. 법적 구속력 여부는 다루지 않습니다.

cards.title: 40,000 sign-ups or six customers: which one is traction?
body: Two founders pitch the same investor in the same week. One makes reusable steel racks for shipping car parts between factories. The other runs a free app for planning team schedules.
The app's slide says 40,000 sign-ups. The rack maker's slide says six customers. The investor calls only one of them back.

image.label: Two pitch slides: 40,000 sign-ups vs six customers
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 왼쪽에 큰 숫자 "40,000"이 적힌 휴대폰 화면, 오른쪽에 철제 운반 랙 옆 작은 숫자 "6". 가운데 투자자의 손이 오른쪽 쪽 전화기를 집어 드는 장면. 실제 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Which founder gets the call?
body: **Rack maker:** six factory customers in its first year. Five placed a second, larger order.
**App:** 40,000 sign-ups after a viral launch. Free to use.
Which shows stronger evidence that customers want the product?

options.text: The app. 40,000 people is a far bigger signal
options.feedback: Big and visible, but a free sign-up costs nothing. It shows people were curious, not that they stayed.

options.text: The rack maker. Customers paid, then came back for more
options.feedback: A second, larger order is hard to fake. It means the racks worked inside the customer's business.

options.text: Neither yet. Six customers is too few to mean anything
options.feedback: Six is small, and investors will notice. But five out of six reordering is a strong pattern, even at small size.

cards.title: Look at who came back.
body: Three months later, the investor asked both founders the same question: how many customers are still buying or using?

groups.label: Still buying or using after 3 months

cards.callout: Five of six factories reordered. About 800 of 40,000 sign-ups still use the app each week.

cards.title: Traction
body: **Traction** is evidence that customers want what you sell, shown by what they do rather than what they say, and growing over time.
It answers an investor's biggest worry: will anyone actually want this? The rack maker had less of everything except that.

image.label: A scale: one heavy reorder outweighs a pile of sign-ups
image.brief: 저울 일러스트. 한쪽에는 가벼운 종이 쪽지 "Sign-ups" 더미가 높이 쌓여 있고, 다른 쪽에는 작은 철제 블록 "Reorder" 하나. 저울은 철제 블록 쪽으로 기울어짐.

cards.title: Not all evidence weighs the same.
body: Investors read signals roughly from weakest to strongest:
list: **Sign-ups and pilots:** free trials, letters of intent (a written promise to consider buying)
**Pull:** customers arrive through referrals, and the line keeps rising
cards.callout: The higher the step, the more it costs a customer to fake.
cards.softwareNote: For apps, the same ladder runs from downloads to weekly use to paid plans to teams adding more seats on their own.

cards.title: Shape matters more than size.
body: A business selling $5,000 a month and growing every month can be more convincing than one stuck at $50,000. Investors fund where a line is going, not just where it is.
The app founder isn't out, either. If those 800 weekly users stay, start paying and bring colleagues, that small group is the real traction. It would make a far better slide than 40,000.

cards.title: Traction can be bought, borrowed or missing for good reasons.
body: Deep discounts and heavy ad spending can create sales that vanish when the spending stops. Ask what customers paid and whether they'd return at full price.
One giant customer can look like traction but is really a risk: lose them and the story ends.
Some products, like new medical devices, can't show sales for years. Then investors weigh other proof, such as test results or the team's track record.

cards.title: Now it's a hot sauce brand.
body: You make hot sauce and have one slide to show traction to an investor. Which number should lead?

options.feedback: Shelf space shows store buyers said yes. It doesn't show shoppers bought, and stores drop slow sellers.

options.text: 70% of stores reordered within eight weeks, with sales per store rising monthly
options.feedback: Reorders mean the sauce sold through to shoppers, and rising sales show the pattern is getting stronger.
Following costs nothing. Without sales linked to it, that's attention, not demand.

cards.title: Traction is proof that's expensive to fake.
body: Lead with what customers did, especially paying again, and show which way the line is moving.
**Try it today:** list the three numbers you'd show an investor or your boss. For each, ask: did this cost the customer anything? Would they do it again?
